# Preface {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-warning title="A work in progress"}
This book is a **work in progress**. It is still under development and will
keep growing and improving over time. Chapters may be revised, expanded, or
reorganized as it is used in the classroom; when something looks unfinished,
that is why. Questions and suggestions are welcome.
:::

**Evidence-Driven Research in AI-era: How to Design, Analyze, Verify, and
Defend** — **EDRAI**, for short — is an open research manual for undergraduate
students in economics, STEM, and business fields who want to turn curiosity
into credible, defensible, evidence-based insight in a world where AI can
produce almost everything. It was first written for an Honors research seminar
at Purdue University, and it is deliberately institution-agnostic: any
instructor or student, anywhere, is welcome to adopt it.

Its one message: *AI is your arm and your research assistant, not your brain.*
You will direct AI tools through the
**Specify → Delegate → Interrogate → Inspect → Verify → Document → Defend**
workflow while keeping every research decision your own. One rule runs through
every verification step in this book: **AI can review AI** — a second model is
a real auditor of the first — **but the last decision is always human**.

Blair, Coppock and Humphreys' *Research Design in the Social Sciences* (RDSS,
free at [book.declaredesign.org](https://book.declaredesign.org)) is the theory
text that EDRAI translates for the undergraduate audience. In the original
course the EDRAI chapter is the **required** reading each week and the matching
RDSS chapters are **recommended** for depth; each chapter's Reading box names
its RDSS companions. Each chapter names a research decision, works an example,
links a Colab lab, shows an AI failure and how to catch it, and asks you to
defend a claim.

The book has six parts: research when AI can produce almost everything;
from curiosity to research design; the research pathways (observational and
experimental, descriptive and causal, and prediction); producing credible
evidence with AI; communicating and defending research; and research after
the conference.

**Languages.** EDRAI is also available in
[Português (Brasil)](../book-pt/index.html) and
[Español](../book-es/index.html). The English edition is the source of truth;
the translations are regenerated from it as it evolves.

If your course runs the flipped format this book supports, most lectures are
led by a student: the day's **Student Research Lead**. That lead's brief lives
at the start of the corresponding lecture notebook, and the appendix
[The Student Research Lead](srl.qmd) collects the format, the preparation
cadence, and the expectations in one place.
